clue.text: Apple without an orange — deranged way of showing love

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the apple wraps around the other letters
deranged means thrown out of order, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: a codling is a variety of cooking apple
taken as written
the opening letter of orange

explanation.surface: A disturbed person spurns an orange in favour of an apple as a way of declaring affection.
explanation.walkthrough: Codling is a traditional English cooking apple; 'without' means outside, so the apple goes around the other letters rather than lacking them.
explanation.definitionFit: Canoodling is kissing and cuddling, an affectionate courting behaviour between lovers.

clue.text: Ready to play in two suits?

parts.note: to match is to suit, the first of two words meaning suit
to fit is also to suit, the second word

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a player in two outfits is ready for the game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two suits' is not clothing: it asks for two verbs each meaning suit, placed one after the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A sportsperson who is match fit has the physical condition required to take part in a competitive game.

clue.text: Extremes in Arab building for market area

indicators.note: in tells us one set of letters sits inside the other
building suggests putting materials together in a new form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: A and Z are the extremes of the alphabet
the letters of Arab rearranged

explanation.surface: An Arab building at its outer limits is used as a trading area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremes in Arab' looks like the first and last letters of Arab; in fact the extremes are A and Z, inserted into a rearranged Arab.
explanation.definitionFit: A bazaar is a Middle Eastern marketplace or a street lined with stalls and shops.

clue.text: Gamble with 10 horses

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ... is a variety of the card game at 10 across, ... poker
second meaning: an establishment of horses kept for breeding

explanation.surface: Someone bets on the horses with ten pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: The 10 is a cross-reference to 10 across, the card game POKER.
explanation.definitionFit: Stud poker is a card game with some cards dealt face up, and a stud is a stable of breeding stallions.

clue.text: In the film fraternity a horse will keep the wolf from the door

definitions.text: will keep the wolf from the door
definitions.note: a verb phrase defining a noun: the person who does this

indicators.note: In shows that the horse goes inside the film company

parts.note: Warner Brothers, the Hollywood studio founded by brothers
taken as written
gee or gee-gee is a childish word for a horse

explanation.surface: In Hollywood circles, a horse is a fine way to avoid poverty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Film fraternity' means a film company of brothers: Warner Bros. A-GEE goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping the wolf from the door means having enough income to stave off hunger, which is what someone in paid work does.

clue.text: Kilns prefabricated to prevent fires?

definitions.note: a verb defined by its purpose; the question mark admits the looseness

indicators.note: fabricated means manufactured or made up, so the letters are assembled in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
the opening three letters of the printed word, split off from the anagram signal

explanation.surface: Factory-made kilns are designed so they will not catch fire.
explanation.walkthrough: The word prefabricated splits: PRE is fodder and 'fabricated' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Water may be scattered in drops over embers or a building to stop flames taking hold, as a sprinkler system does.

clue.text: Songs inspired by Bacchus disguised as Loki

indicators.note: something disguised has its appearance changed, so these letters take a new form

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The trickster god Loki dresses up and sings drinking songs to the wine god.
explanation.walkthrough: Loki is the Norse trickster famous for disguises, which makes the anagram signal apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Skolia were ancient Greek drinking songs sung in turn at banquets, wine being the gift of Bacchus.

clue.text: St Paul's little bird

definitions.note: the possessive names the cathedral's architect
definitions.meaning: first meaning: Sir Christopher ... designed St Paul's Cathedral in London
second meaning: a tiny brown songbird

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a bird belonging to the saint; the possessive actually means the man whose building St Paul's is.
explanation.definitionFit: The architect of the London cathedral shares his surname with a small songbird with a cocked tail.

clue.text: A celebration with act I missed out of the Milky Way

indicators.note: missed suggests the letters went astray, so they are not in their written order

parts.note: taken as written
a gala is a festive celebration
the letters of act I rearranged

explanation.surface: A gala performance misses its first act and has nothing to do with the galaxy.
explanation.walkthrough: The Milky Way looks astronomical; here it is literal, a supply of milk, so 'out of' it means lacking milk.
explanation.definitionFit: Agalactia is the medical term for a mother's failure to produce breast milk after giving birth.

clue.text: Gamble with fire

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a card game played for stakes
second meaning: the metal rod used to stir the coals of a fire

explanation.surface: Someone takes a dangerous risk, playing with fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gamble with fire' sounds like playing with fire; 'with fire' means the tool used with a fire.
explanation.definitionFit: Poker is a betting card game, and also the iron bar kept beside a hearth for stirring burning coals.

clue.text: Where to find fruit is a whale of a problem

parts.note: an orc is a killer whale, the orca
hard means difficult, a problem to solve

explanation.surface: Finding fruit is said to be a huge difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A whale of a' looks like the idiom for a great deal; it is split to give a whale and a difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchard is a plot of land planted with fruit trees such as apples or pears.

clue.text: Alien's not first fiddle, being yellow

indicators.note: not first tells us to drop the opening letter of the following word

parts.note: ET is the alien of the Spielberg film
a fiddle is a violin

explanation.surface: An extraterrestrial plays second fiddle and is too cowardly to lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not first fiddle' sounds like second fiddle, but it means fiddle without its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Etiolin is the yellowish pigment found in plants grown in darkness, which are pale and etiolated.

clue.text: See 21 down
Gamble with Jolly Roger, not the thief of tarts

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the card game also called pontoon or twenty-one

definitions.text: Jolly Roger, not the thief of tarts
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the pirate flag, a ..., unlike the red Knave of Hearts who stole the tarts

explanation.surface: Pirates gamble, but none of them is the nursery-rhyme tart thief.
explanation.walkthrough: A jack is a flag and also a knave; the Knave of Hearts in the nursery rhyme is a red jack, the pirate flag a black one.
explanation.definitionFit: Blackjack is the casino card game aiming for twenty-one, and a black jack is a pirate's black ensign.

clue.text: Late buzzer keeps little boy pursuing deer

indicators.note: keeps means holds inside, so the buzzer surrounds the rest

parts.note: a bee is an insect that buzzes

indicators.note: pursuing means following behind, so the boy comes after the deer

parts.note: a hind is a female deer
Tim, short for Timothy, as in Tiny Tim

explanation.surface: A tardy bee holds a small boy who is chasing a deer.
explanation.definitionFit: Being behind time means running later than scheduled or expected, overdue.

clue.text: Short of bags for the kennel — dog's tail wagging

definitions.note: describes trousers cut short, bags being trousers

indicators.note: wagging means moving to and fro, so these letters are shaken into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a tail is the hindmost part, so take the final letter of that word

parts.note: the closing letter of dog

explanation.surface: A dog wags its tail because the kennel is missing some bags.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bags' is old British slang for loose trousers, as in Oxford bags; 'Short of' means not lacking but cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: Trousers that stop at the knee are short ones, so knee-length describes bags cut down in size.

clue.text: Identical junction — bale out

indicators.note: out suggests something put out of place, so those letters are rearranged

parts.note: a road interchange is a motorway junction
the letters of bale rearranged

explanation.surface: At a twin road junction a hay bale has fallen out of a lorry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bale out' looks like escaping by parachute; it is the word bale and its anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that can be swapped for each other without difference are effectively alike, the same in function.

clue.text: Gamble and suffer, in a way

indicators.note: in shows one word goes inside the other

parts.note: a route is a way
to suffer in the old sense is to allow, to let

explanation.surface: Gambling and suffering go together, in a manner of speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suffer' is in its biblical sense of permit, as in 'suffer the little children'; 'in a way' looks like 'in some sense'.
explanation.definitionFit: Roulette is the casino game of chance played on a spinning wheel with a ball.

clue.text: Gamble on vehicle that's raised the gold standard

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means read upwards, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: a cab is a vehicle, a taxi
the carat is the measure of gold purity

explanation.surface: Someone bets on a car that has raised the bar for quality.
explanation.definitionFit: Baccarat is a card game played in casinos in which players bet on banker or player hands.

clue.text: Where fuel comes from for bus being repaired in store

indicators.note: something being repaired is taken apart and put back, so these letters are reassembled
in shows that these letters go inside the next word

parts.note: to garner is to store, as grain
the letters of bus rearranged

explanation.surface: A bus in the depot workshop gets its fuel from a particular place.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged bus goes inside GARNER after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A gas burner is the nozzle or jet on a cooker where the gas emerges and is lit.

clue.text: Male or female heavyweight grave digger

parts.note: male or female is a person's sex
a ton is a heavy weight

explanation.surface: A heavy man or woman digs graves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heavyweight grave digger' reads as a burly worker; heavyweight is a weight unit of its own.
explanation.definitionFit: A sexton is a church officer whose duties traditionally included digging graves in the churchyard.

clue.text: A number of parasites returned to Salisbury

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the letters are read from the end

parts.note: lice are parasitic insects
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: Some parasites have been sent back to the cathedral city.
explanation.walkthrough: Salisbury looks like the city; it is the title of the Marquess of Salisbury, family name Cecil, a Victorian Prime Minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Cecil, third Marquess of Salisbury, was British Prime Minister three times, so his surname stands for the title.

clue.text: Gamble to c-confine delay

parts.note: the stammered letter of the next word
to hem in is to confine
to defer is to delay

explanation.surface: A stammering gambler tries to hold back a delay.
explanation.walkthrough: The stutter c-confine supplies an extra C before the synonym for confine.
explanation.definitionFit: Chemin de fer is a casino card game, a form of baccarat, whose name is French for railway.

clue.text: Shrub at country house, the coach-driver's place

parts.note: box is an evergreen shrub used for hedges
a country seat is a grand house on an estate

explanation.surface: A shrub grows at a country estate where the coachman sits.
explanation.definitionFit: The box seat is the elevated bench at the front of a horse-drawn coach where the driver sits.

clue.text: Gamble and bluster

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a British card game similar to poker

explanation.definitionFit: Brag is an old three-card betting game ancestral to poker, and to talk big and boastfully.

clue.text: Stars concealed in wheat?

indicators.note: concealed suggests the letters are muddled up so they cannot be seen as written

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Something starry is lurking in a field of wheat.
explanation.walkthrough: A wain is a farm wagon that would carry wheat, which makes the surface fit; Charles's Wain is the constellation also called the Plough.
explanation.definitionFit: The Wain is a traditional name for the seven bright stars of the Plough or Big Dipper.

clue.text: Premier traveller to America?

parts.note: surface reading: the first person to journey to the New World
setter's reading: the Prime Minister of 2002, forever flying over to see the US President

explanation.walkthrough: Premier looks like an adjective meaning first; it is a noun, the British Prime Minister, known by his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: In 2002 Britain's Prime Minister was Mr Blair, famous for frequent trips to Washington.

clue.text: A fight, more or less

parts.note: taken as written
a bout is a boxing match or fight

explanation.surface: A fight, roughly speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: About means approximately, roughly, near enough, as in about ten people.

clue.text: Friar I am unable to reform?

parts.note: to mend one's ways is to reform
I am unable means I can't

explanation.surface: A friar confesses he cannot change his ways.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces come in reverse order to the clue: the word for reform comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Mendicant orders such as Franciscans and Dominicans were friars who lived by begging for alms.
